steps.label: Trachea and central bronchi
steps.detail: Follow the trachea and main and lobar bronchi for narrowing, intraluminal material and extrinsic compression.
steps.look: Thin-section axial images with multiplanar and minimum-intensity projections along the airway.
steps.normal: Trachea and central bronchi patent with normal calibre and wall.
findings: Tracheal stenosis at [ ], __ mm long, minimum lumen __ mm (post-intubation pattern).
Endobronchial lesion in the [ ] bronchus.
Circumferential wall thickening sparing the posterior membrane (relapsing polychondritis / tracheobronchopathia pattern).
steps.tip: Diseases of the cartilage spare the posterior membrane; dependent mucus can mimic an endobronchial lesion.

steps.label: Bronchiectasis
steps.detail: Describe distribution and morphology, lack of tapering and bronchi visible near the pleura.
steps.look: Compare each bronchus with its accompanying artery (signet ring); follow bronchi to the periphery.
findings: [Cylindrical / varicose / cystic] bronchiectasis in the [ ] lobes.
Traction bronchiectasis within fibrosis.
steps.tip: Traction bronchiectasis belongs to the surrounding fibrosis and is interpreted with it.

steps.label: Small airways
steps.detail: Map centrilobular nodules, tree-in-bud change and mucus plugging.
steps.look: Lung windows in the periphery.
steps.normal: No tree-in-bud or centrilobular nodules; no mucus plugging.
findings: Tree-in-bud nodules in the [ ], compatible with infectious bronchiolitis.
Mucus plugging of the [ ] bronchi.

steps.label: Expiratory imaging
steps.detail: Assess air trapping and dynamic central airway collapse when expiratory images are acquired.
steps.look: Paired inspiratory and expiratory images at the same levels.
steps.normal: Expiration: [adequate / limited / not acquired]. Air trapping: [not assessed / none / distribution]. Dynamic central airway collapse: [not assessed / findings].
findings: Lobular air trapping in the [ ].
Expiratory collapse of the trachea by more than __%.
Expiratory imaging not acquired; air trapping not assessed.
steps.tip: Mosaic attenuation can reflect air trapping, vascular disease or infiltrates; expiration separates them.

steps.label: Consequences
steps.detail: Look for collapse, post-obstructive infection and an obstructing mass.
steps.look: Lobes distal to a narrowed airway.
steps.normal: No atelectasis, consolidation or obstructing mass.
findings: [Right upper lobe] collapse distal to an obstructing lesion.
Post-obstructive consolidation.

steps.label: Projection and quality
steps.detail: Record actual source projection, position, acquisition/coverage and quality; distinguish technical limitations and artefacts from disease.
steps.look: Confirm actual AP/PA/lateral or other view and erect/supine/decubitus position from source data; assess rotation, inspiration, penetration, motion, clipping, artefacts and source scaling. No view is assumed present.
findings: AP supine radiograph; heart size cannot be assessed reliably.
Rotated to the [right]; mediastinal contours are distorted.
Poor inspiration; basal opacity may be exaggerated.
steps.tip: Technical correction, crop or annotation removal can change source presentation; preserve original source and disclose processing. An unavailable or limited view is not an adequately assessed negative study.

steps.label: Airway, mediastinum, hila and heart
steps.detail: Inspect every covered airway, hilar, mediastinal and cardiac silhouette/interface with source projection limits; do not infer resolved chamber/wall anatomy or physiology from overlap.
steps.look: Inspect trachea/carinal/main bronchial region, both hila, cardiac borders, aortic/pulmonary/caval contours, mediastinal lines/recesses and retrosternal/retrocardiac regions. Silhouette loss is a projected interface clue; correlate views only if acquired.
findings: Cardiomegaly (cardiothoracic ratio __ on a PA film).
Enlarged [right / bilateral] hilum.
Widened superior mediastinum.
Obliterated aortopulmonary window.
steps.tip: CTR interpretation requires the actual method and projection; AP/supine magnification or poor inspiration must not be treated as standard PA size. Silhouette enlargement does not measure pressure, EF, shunt or establish a unique cause.

steps.label: Lungs
steps.detail: Describe each actual pulmonary opacity/lucency, vascular or volume-change pattern and covered regional extent; assess hidden and overlapping areas with appropriate uncertainty.
steps.look: Inspect apices, perihilar/retrocardiac and subdiaphragmatic lung, every covered zone and any supported lobar/localisation signs. Describe each consolidation/interstitial/nodular/mass/lucent or volume-loss component and actual air bronchogram/fissural/hilar displacement without assuming one cause.
findings: Consolidation in the [right middle lobe] with loss of the [right heart border] (silhouette sign).
Upper-lobe venous diversion, Kerley B lines and peribronchial cuffing (interstitial oedema).
Solitary pulmonary nodule __ mm in the [ ].
Lobar collapse of the [left lower lobe] (sail sign behind the heart).
steps.tip: Consolidation, oedema, infection, haemorrhage, collapse and malignancy can overlap. Air bronchograms or projected volume-loss signs support a differential, not unique pathology or microscopic confirmation.

steps.label: Pleura and diaphragm
steps.detail: Assess each actually visible pleural/diaphragmatic/recess interface and complication, with projection/position-dependent visibility and source limits.
steps.look: Assess both apices, lateral/posterior costophrenic regions if obtained, fissural/subpulmonic compartments, pleural lines and diaphragmatic contours. Supine air/fluid distribution differs from erect views. Distinguish skinfolds, bullae and other mimics with source confidence.
findings: [Right] pleural effusion with a meniscus.
[Left] apical pneumothorax with a visible pleural line, __ cm at the apex.
Deep sulcus sign on a supine radiograph (anterior pneumothorax).
Free gas beneath the right hemidiaphragm.
steps.tip: An inconspicuous pneumothorax/effusion on a limited/supine film is not exclusion. Do not derive an exact fluid volume, tension physiology or fluid chemistry from one projection. Free gas/urgent findings require actual source and clinical assessment.

steps.label: Devices, bones and review areas
steps.detail: Trace each actually present device and inspect all covered osseous/soft-tissue/upper-abdominal review regions; record full obtained route/tip/landmark relation and unresolved extent.
steps.look: Trace each airway/enteric/vascular/drain/device route, tip and visible ports against actual landmarks; note device type, acquisition time and any position-dependent uncertainty. Review each covered rib/clavicle/scapula/vertebral/sternal region, joints, chest-wall/breast/neck soft tissue and visible upper abdomen.
findings: Endotracheal tube tip __ cm above the carina.
Central venous catheter tip in the [ ].
Nasogastric tube coiled in the oesophagus — reposition before use.
Rib fractures of the [ ] ribs.
steps.tip: No device or complication is asserted absent until actual covered sources are assessed. Projected tip distances require named landmarks, phase/position and calibration; lumen/wall/3D course and dynamic function may remain unresolved.

model.reporting_aim: Partial thoracic orientation only. This companion does not supply actual patient projection geometry, all native hilar/mediastinal/pleural interfaces, every rib/joint/soft tissue, disease/device3D routes or cardiac/respiratory function. Report actual acquired sources; unresolved or uncovered anatomy remains unassessed.

steps.label: Parenchymal pattern
steps.detail: Describe ground glass, consolidation, crazy paving and associated vascular or septal changes.
steps.look: Thin-section lung windows.
findings: Multifocal ground-glass opacities with crazy paving.
Ground glass with vascular enlargement within the opacities.
Organising pattern: consolidation with subpleural bands and reversed halo.

steps.label: Distribution and extent
steps.detail: Map laterality, lobes and peripheral or central predominance; estimate extent.
steps.look: Coronal reformats; score each lobe for extent.
findings: Bilateral, peripheral and lower-lobe predominant.
CT involvement score __/25.
Unilateral central distribution.
steps.tip: Bilateral, peripheral, multifocal ground glass is the typical distribution.

steps.label: Features favouring another cause
steps.detail: Seek findings supporting another process.
steps.look: Tree-in-bud, cavitation, lobar consolidation, effusions, septal lines and cardiomegaly.
steps.normal: No features to suggest an alternative diagnosis.
findings: Tree-in-bud and centrilobular nodules (bronchopneumonia pattern).
Septal thickening with effusions and cardiomegaly (oedema pattern).
Lobar consolidation.

steps.label: Associated findings
steps.detail: Review pleura, nodes and complications such as pulmonary embolism when contrast was given.
steps.look: Pleural spaces, mediastinum and pulmonary arteries if opacified.
findings: Pulmonary embolism in the [ ] arteries.
Pneumomediastinum.
Mediastinal lymphadenopathy.

steps.label: Comparison and CO-RADS
steps.detail: State interval change and, when appropriate for the setting, the CO-RADS category with its supporting pattern.
steps.look: Prior imaging; the clinical context in which CO-RADS applies.
findings: CO-RADS 5: typical features.
CO-RADS 3: equivocal features.
CO-RADS 2: features typical of another infection.
Interval [improvement / progression] since [date].
steps.tip: CO-RADS expresses suspicion in its intended setting and does not confirm infection.

steps.label: Cyst morphology
steps.detail: Trace each actual cyst or cyst-like lesion through obtained source planes; describe wall, contents, shape, septa, mural components and airway/vessel continuity with source uncertainty.
steps.look: Use original thin sections and matching reformats, multiple windows, stated reconstruction/calibration and local axes. Distinguish cysts from cavities, bullae/emphysema, pneumatoceles, honeycombing and cystic bronchiectasis; do not infer epithelial lining or microscopic wall layers from CT.
findings: Round thin-walled cysts __–__ mm, uniformly distributed (LAM pattern).
Bizarre-shaped cysts with nodules (Langerhans cell histiocytosis pattern).
Lentiform subpleural and paramediastinal cysts (Birt–Hogg–Dubé pattern).
steps.tip: Wall thickness or apparent absence alone is not a diagnostic cutoff; partial volume, reconstruction and orientation affect thin walls. Thick/irregular components and a cyst-like cavity require a stated differential.

steps.label: Distribution
steps.detail: Record actual count/extent and regional distribution across every covered lobe, axial compartment, pleural recess and fissural/mediastinal interface; identify coverage limits.
steps.look: Inspect each actual covered side/lobe/region and variant: apical/basal, central/peripheral, peribronchovascular, subpleural/paramediastinal and interlobar relationships. Representative pictures cannot establish full cyst count or exclusion of disease elsewhere.
findings: Upper-zone predominance with sparing of the costophrenic angles.
Diffuse distribution including the bases.
Lower-zone, subpleural and paramediastinal predominance.
steps.tip: The source four-cysts/age-forty rule is a contextual heuristic, not a diagnosis or exclusion rule, particularly with recurrent pneumothorax or suspected hereditary disease. Costophrenic distribution supports a differential, not a unique diagnosis.

steps.label: Associated nodules
steps.detail: Describe each solid/cavitating nodule, mural or intracystic component and its relationship to cysts, airways and vessels; assess actual prior change.
steps.look: Record wall nodularity/irregular thickening, intracystic material, traversing vessels and adjacent nodules/masses. Trace airway continuity and assess prior source images at matched sites without assuming registration.
findings: Centrilobular and cavitating nodules in the upper zones.
steps.tip: New/growing mural solid tissue or changing cyst-associated nodules warrant appropriate clinical evaluation. Wall thinning or low/negative PET uptake alone does not establish benignity; no PET finding is borrowed when PET was not obtained.

steps.label: Background lung
steps.detail: Describe intervening parenchyma, ground glass, septa, reticulation, fibrosis, honeycombing, emphysema and airway change with source phase and differential.
steps.look: Assess every covered regional airway/interstitial/vascular interface. Expiratory air trapping, perfusion and dynamic behaviour require those actually acquired sources; inspiratory CT alone does not provide them.
findings: Ground glass with perivascular cysts (LIP pattern).
Ground glass with small cysts (DIP pattern).
steps.tip: LAM/BHD-FDS/PLCH/LIP/AMP-DIP patterns overlap with infection, neoplasia, deposition and other causes. Record morphology and uncertainty; source terminology does not prove histology, genotype or functional severity.

steps.label: Context and complications
steps.detail: Review pleura, pneumothorax/fluid, covered nodes and systemic findings; separate observed CT from supplied history, genetics, microbiology or tissue evidence.
steps.look: Assess actual pleura/recesses, mediastinal/hilar nodes and covered upper abdominal organs. Renal, cutaneous, genetic, infection and smoking/autoimmune context must come from supplied current source/history, not the teaching-case diagnosis.
findings: Pneumothorax on the [ ].
Renal angiomyolipomas in the upper abdomen (tuberous sclerosis / LAM).
Renal lesion in the upper abdomen (Birt–Hogg–Dubé context).
steps.tip: No pneumothorax, chylous fluid, renal tumour, systemic disease or hereditary finding may be asserted from unassessed anatomy. CT fluid is not proven chyle; urgency depends on actual findings and clinical context.

model.reporting_aim: Partial thoracic orientation only. This companion does not supply individual patient cysts, microscopic walls, complete airway/vessel interfaces, lobar/segmental disease distribution, mural nodules, genotype, histology or dynamic function. Report actual acquired sources; missing anatomy remains unassessed.

steps.label: Lumen and calibre
steps.detail: Map every acquired cervical, thoracic and abdominal esophageal component and EGJ/hiatal relationship; describe actual lumen, contents and recorded transit with source coverage and uncertainty.
steps.look: Trace the full obtained pharyngoesophageal-to-gastric course and every lumen/content component, including actual diverticular or duplicated routes. Describe cervical/thoracic/abdominal site, distension, axes/calibration, EGJ relative to diaphragm and acquired gastric extent. Compare recorded bolus clearance only at actual source times and positions. VFSS esophageal screening does not constitute a complete dedicated esophagram; CT or static MRI does not provide cine transit or sphincter pressure.
findings: Actual acquired lumen and calibre finding/interface [ ]; source site/side, modality/projection/phase/time and extent [ ]; supplied context, differential and unassessed evidence [ ].
steps.tip: A retained column or distal bird-beak pattern is a source observation; the clinical diagnosis and subtype use applicable complementary tests and context. A selected still, screening pass or static surface does not certify normal clearance, sphincter relaxation or absence of aspiration.

steps.label: Wall and mucosa
steps.detail: Trace every source-resolved wall, mucosal surface and actual lesion component; retain layer, ulcer, gland/duct, neural and vascular interfaces as required anatomy while keeping unresolved microscopic tissue and identity explicit.
steps.look: Review obtained fluoroscopic single/double-contrast surface detail, CT/MRI wall and extramural interfaces, and separately supplied endoscopic/EUS or pathological evidence. Map actual fold, plaque, erosion, ulcer, intramural/exophytic/intraluminal component, stalk and each adjacent interface. Wall layers, glands/ducts and neural/vascular plexuses remain required but unproven unless their actual source resolution and independent review support them; a whole-esophagus mask is not every layer.
findings: Actual acquired wall and mucosa finding/interface [ ]; source site/side, modality/projection/phase/time and extent [ ]; supplied context, differential and unassessed evidence [ ].
steps.tip: Plaques, ulceration, wall thickening or a reticular surface do not independently prove an organism, Barrett metaplasia, dysplasia or tumour histology. Supplied endoscopic sampling/pathology and applicable diagnostic framework stay separate; static imaging does not resolve every microscopic layer.

steps.label: Rings, webs and strictures
steps.detail: Inventory every actual ring, web, bar, stricture, pouch or communication with source site, boundary and passage effect; morphology alone does not supply cause, pressure, histology or an intervention decision.
steps.look: Use actual distended source views for each narrowing, with site, minimum lumen, length, circumferential extent, contour, upstream contents and acquired passage. For every pouch map neck, wall, retained content and communication. Record whether an apparent ring/bar persists across obtained frames. Tapering, shouldering or calcification has a differential; pseudoachalasia, inflammation, treatment and neoplasia are not ruled out by smooth contour.
findings: Actual acquired rings, webs and strictures finding/interface [ ]; source site/side, modality/projection/phase/time and extent [ ]; supplied context, differential and unassessed evidence [ ].
steps.tip: Smooth tapered narrowing is not proof of benignity, and shouldering is not a unique carcinoma diagnosis. Distension and projection alter apparent calibre; one unacquired or inadequately distended segment cannot be supplied as negative.

steps.label: External impressions
steps.detail: Trace all acquired esophageal relationships to actual vessels, airways, neural routes, nodes, mediastinal tissues and hiatus/stomach; distinguish source contact or impression from supported invasion or physiological causation.
steps.look: Trace each actual acquired arterial/venous course and branch, including variant arches/subclavian or pulmonary routes, vessel wall/lumen and intervening tissues. Review trachea/bronchi, left atrium/pericardium, mediastinal compartments, nodes, pleura, spine and neural/lymphatic connections. Map diaphragm/crura, phrenoesophageal attachments, EGJ, herniated stomach/other contents and rotation with coverage limits. Preserve every source variant and treated route rather than substituting a generic vascular or hiatal model.
findings: Actual acquired external impressions finding/interface [ ]; source site/side, modality/projection/phase/time and extent [ ]; supplied context, differential and unassessed evidence [ ].
steps.tip: External contact, absent visible fat plane or a vascular impression alone does not establish invasion, flow direction, pressure or symptom causation. A hiatal hernia or observed reflux is not alone a diagnosis of GERD or an automatic operative indication.

steps.label: Acute complications
steps.detail: Map each actual injury, leak, fistula, intramural dissection, collection and treated/device interface, with acquired spread and timing; document concerning findings, negative-study limits and actual clinical communication.
steps.look: Identify actual source injury level/circumference, wall defect or intramural tract, extraluminal contrast/material, air/fluid and connections to mediastinum, pleura, lung, airway or abdomen. Record the contrast type/route, pre/postcontrast or fluoroscopic acquisition, timing, obtained extent and artifacts. Review each actual anastomosis, conduit, myotomy/fundoplication region, stent, tube or drain and comparison; management depends on the supplied clinical setting and relevant team, not a templated lesion label.
findings: Actual acquired acute complications finding/interface [ ]; source site/side, modality/projection/phase/time and extent [ ]; supplied context, differential and unassessed evidence [ ].
steps.tip: No extravasation on a limited contrast study does not exclude every perforation. Pneumomediastinum, fluid or wall thickening has a differential; anatomical side or a historical pattern is not a compulsory injury site or a unique causal diagnosis.

model.reporting_aim: Partial esophageal orientation only. This static schematic does not contain every native cervical/thoracic/abdominal wall layer, gland/duct, neural/vascular/lymphatic branch, mucosal lesion, pouch/hiatal/gastric or treated interface. It supplies no acquired transit, sphincter pressure/relaxation, reflux diagnosis, histology, complete leak exclusion or treatment effect.

steps.label: Dominant pattern
steps.detail: Describe every actual dominant and associated ground-glass, consolidative, nodular, reticular/cystic or other pattern with source-defined site, extent, tissue interfaces and quality.
steps.look: Inspect thin source sections and multiple windows/reformats. Distinguish reticular septa from non-fibrotic thickening, ground glass from vessel-obscuring consolidation, cyst/mimic and every solid or airspace component. Dependent density and incomplete inspiration can simulate disease.
findings: Reticular pattern with honeycombing.
Nodular pattern with [perilymphatic / centrilobular / random] distribution.
Ground-glass opacity with [crazy paving / mosaic attenuation].
Low attenuation: [centrilobular emphysema / cysts].
steps.tip: Ground glass alone is not fibrosis, unique inflammation, infection or a specific histology. Motion, under-inspiration, window/reconstruction and partial volume may alter apparent pattern and thin tissue borders.

steps.label: Distribution
steps.detail: Record all covered side/lobe/segment and secondary-lobule/axial/pleural relationships with actual regional distribution and variant/coverage limits.
steps.look: Trace every covered lobe/actual segment and variant, central/peripheral/subpleural/peribronchovascular/perilobular compartments, fissures, pleural recesses and source-resolved secondary lobules. Identify centrilobular, perilymphatic or random nodular patterns without borrowing invisible microscopic anatomy.
findings: Basal and subpleural predominance.
Upper-zone and peribronchovascular predominance.
Subpleural sparing (NSIP pattern).
steps.tip: A representative still cannot establish whole-lung disease absence, burden or a microscopic lobular map. State mixed patterns, each actual region and unassessed coverage.

steps.label: Fibrosis
steps.detail: Describe each source fibrosis, distortion, traction airway, honeycomb and volume-loss component; separate the CT pattern from aetiological/multidisciplinary diagnosis.
steps.look: Assess actual irregular inter/intralobular septa, distortion, displacement, traction bronchi/bronchioles and honeycomb versus mimics. Review all spatial gradients and alternative/mixed features before naming UIP/probable UIP/indeterminate/alternative under a stated reference; valid unclassifiable morphology remains explicit.
findings: UIP pattern: basal subpleural honeycombing with traction bronchiectasis.
Probable UIP: basal subpleural reticulation with traction bronchiectasis, no honeycombing.
Fibrosis with features of an alternative diagnosis: [ ].
steps.tip: A CT UIP pattern does not equal idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis; secondary causes and multidisciplinary confidence matter. Honeycombing can overlap other fibrotic diseases; CT appearance is not the histological definition.

steps.label: Airways and air trapping
steps.detail: Trace actual airway and regional mosaic changes; describe expiratory/prone findings only from those acquired phases with technique and source uncertainty.
steps.look: Trace luminal/wall changes and airway-artery relationships across actual planes. Mosaic attenuation may be airway, vascular or infiltrative; a three-density appearance on inspiration does not supply an expiratory study. Compare inspiration/expiration/prone only when actually acquired.
findings: Lobular air trapping on expiration with mosaic attenuation (hypersensitivity pneumonitis pattern with fibrosis).
Expiratory imaging not acquired.
steps.tip: Do not assert no air trapping on an unperformed expiration or resolution on an unperformed prone scan. Air trapping/mosaicism alone does not uniquely diagnose HP; bronchiolocentric features can have other causes.

steps.label: Comparison and context
steps.detail: Compare actual matching source sites and methods; report complications and supplied clinical/physiological context without inferring progression, pressure or function from a still.
steps.look: Record prior date/coverage/phase/reconstruction and comparable sites, symptoms and PFT dates/values if supplied. Review acute opacity, pleural/mediastinal air or fluid, nodes, masses and covered vascular/systemic clues with alternative causes.
findings: Progression of fibrosis since [date].
Dilated oesophagus (systemic sclerosis context).
Pleural plaques (asbestos exposure).
steps.tip: CT progression alone does not establish PPF. The named2022 definition uses at least two of symptoms/radiology/physiology within one year, no alternative explanation, in fibrotic ILD other than IPF. Preserve actual dates and sources; new acute opacity is not unique for exacerbation.

model.reporting_aim: Partial thoracic orientation only. This companion does not supply source patient fibrosis, microscopic lobules/septa, full native airway/vessel/lymphatic walls, honeycomb/lesion geometry, regional disease burden or acquired respiratory/physiological change. Report actual source images; missing anatomy remains unassessed.

steps.label: Primary tumour
steps.detail: Record site, total size and, for a part-solid lesion, the solid component.
steps.look: Lung windows in the plane of maximal extent; measure the solid component separately in part-solid tumours.
findings: [Solid] tumour in the [right upper lobe], __ mm.
Part-solid lesion __ mm with a solid component of __ mm (T category by solid component).
steps.tip: In part-solid tumours the T category depends on the solid (invasive) component size.

steps.label: Local extent (T descriptors)
steps.detail: Check airway involvement, atelectasis, pleura, chest wall, mediastinum and separate nodules.
steps.look: Soft-tissue and lung windows; relation to the main bronchus, carina, pleura and mediastinal structures.
findings: Involvement of the main bronchus without carina involvement, with atelectasis to the hilum (T2).
Chest wall invasion (T3).
Invasion of the mediastinum / great vessels / carina (T4).
Separate nodule in the same lobe (T3) / different ipsilateral lobe (T4).

steps.label: Regional nodes
steps.detail: Name suspicious stations and laterality; separate single-station from multiple-station N2 disease.
steps.look: IASLC nodal map; short axis at each station.
steps.normal: No suspicious hilar or mediastinal nodes.
findings: Ipsilateral hilar node (N1).
Single ipsilateral mediastinal station [4R] (N2a).
Multiple ipsilateral mediastinal stations (N2b).
Contralateral mediastinal or supraclavicular node (N3).
steps.tip: Station 1 (supraclavicular) nodes are N3 on either side.

steps.label: Distant disease
steps.detail: Inspect pleura, pericardium, contralateral lung, adrenals, liver and imaged bones.
steps.look: Pleural surfaces; adrenals and liver on the upper abdominal coverage; bones.
steps.normal: No pleural, contralateral lung or extrathoracic metastases in the field.
findings: Pleural nodules / malignant effusion (M1a).
Single extrathoracic metastasis in the [adrenal] (M1b).
Multiple extrathoracic metastases in [one / several] organ systems (M1c1 / M1c2).

steps.label: Imaging stage
steps.detail: Summarise imaging T, N and M with the TNM edition and the findings whose confirmation would change stage.
steps.look: Combine the descriptors above; name the edition.
findings: Clinical imaging stage (TNM 9th edition): cT__ cN__ cM__.
Stage depends on confirmation of [ ] by [EBUS / PET-CT / biopsy].

steps.label: Compartment
steps.detail: Localise the lesion to the prevascular, visceral or paravertebral compartment.
steps.look: Axial and sagittal images; the epicentre defines the compartment.
findings: Prevascular (anterior) mediastinal mass __ × __ mm.
Visceral (middle) mediastinal mass.
Paravertebral (posterior) mass extending into the neural foramen.
steps.tip: Localise the epicentre first; each compartment has its own differential.

steps.label: Composition
steps.detail: Assess soft tissue, fluid, fat, calcification and enhancement.
steps.look: CT attenuation before and after contrast.
findings: Fluid-attenuation cyst with a thin wall (e.g., bronchogenic or pericardial cyst).
Fat, fluid and calcification (teratoma pattern).
Homogeneous soft-tissue mass with enhancement.

steps.label: Local relationships
steps.detail: Assess displacement or invasion of vessels, airway and oesophagus.
steps.look: Fat planes around the mass; vessel and airway calibre.
steps.normal: No compression or invasion of adjacent structures.
findings: Compression of the superior vena cava.
Tracheal displacement / narrowing.
Invasion of the pericardium.

steps.label: Nodal stations
steps.detail: Identify involved nodal stations and morphology.
steps.look: IASLC map: stations 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10; short axis.
steps.normal: No enlarged mediastinal or hilar nodes.
findings: Enlarged nodes in stations [4R, 7], short axis up to __ mm.
Necrotic nodes.
Calcified nodes.
steps.tip: Assign stations by their anatomic landmarks, not by proximity to a large vessel.

steps.label: Other thoracic findings
steps.detail: Review lungs, pleura, spinal canal and chest wall extension.
steps.look: Lung windows; neural foramina for paravertebral masses.
findings: Extension into the spinal canal through the neural foramen.
Pleural deposits.

steps.label: Pathway
steps.detail: Choose the incidental, screening or known-malignancy pathway and check exclusions.
steps.look: Referral context: age, cancer history, immune status and screening programme.
findings: Incidental nodule in a patient aged __ without cancer or immunosuppression: Fleischner 2017 applies.
Screening context: the programme protocol applies, not Fleischner.
Known malignancy: follow the oncology context, not Fleischner.
steps.tip: Fleischner guidance does not apply to screening, patients under 35, immunocompromise or known cancer.

steps.label: Nodule type and location
steps.detail: Record location and whether each nodule is solid, pure ground glass or part-solid.
steps.look: Thin sections (1.5 mm or less); lung windows.
findings: Solid nodule in the [right upper lobe] (series __ image __).
Pure ground-glass nodule in the [ ].
Part-solid nodule in the [ ].

steps.label: Size and morphology
steps.detail: Measure mean diameter or volume and assess margins, fat, calcification and perifissural shape.
steps.look: Average of long and short axes in the plane of maximal dimension; bone window for calcification.
findings: Solid nodule, mean diameter __ mm, [smooth / lobulated / spiculated].
Benign calcification pattern ([diffuse / central / laminated / popcorn]).
Intranodular fat (hamartoma).
Perifissural nodule: smooth, triangular or lentiform, attached to the fissure.
steps.tip: A perifissural nodule needs the complete benign morphology, not only proximity to a fissure.

steps.label: Interval change
steps.detail: Compare with prior CT using comparable reconstructions.
steps.look: Same slice thickness and kernel; volumetry when available.
findings: Stable since [date] (__ years).
Growth from __ to __ mm since [date].
New solid component in a previously pure ground-glass nodule.

steps.label: Assessment and recommendation
steps.detail: Identify the most suspicious nodule and give a recommendation with the guideline and its rationale.
steps.look: Apply the chosen guideline to the most suspicious nodule.
findings: Solid nodule under 6 mm in a low-risk patient: no routine follow-up (Fleischner 2017).
Solid nodule 6–8 mm: CT at 6–12 months (Fleischner 2017).
Nodule over 8 mm: consider CT at 3 months, PET-CT or tissue sampling.

steps.label: Parenchyma
steps.detail: Record every actual consolidation/nodule/cavity or other parenchymal component, source site/extent and quality, with a supported differential.
steps.look: Review actual radiographic/CT or other acquired sources with appropriate projection/reconstruction/windows and coverage. Trace each visible lesion, wall/content, associated airway/vessel/pleural relation and mimics. A teaching-case diagnosis does not describe the current patient.
findings: Upper-lobe consolidation with cavitation __ mm (post-primary pattern).
Consolidation in the [ ] with ipsilateral hilar lymphadenopathy (primary pattern).
steps.tip: Cavitation, consolidation, nodules or an apparent fungal-ball component are not unique TB or independently proven microbiology. Missing or limited views cannot be negative disease evidence.

steps.label: Spread pattern
steps.detail: Describe actually resolved airway-centred, random/miliary or other distribution and acquired regional extent; do not infer unique organism or microscopic spread from morphology.
steps.look: Assess every covered side/lobe/region and source-resolved bronchiolar/lobular relationships. Tree-in-bud and random nodules have multiple causes; small lesions may be unresolved on radiography and better depicted on actual CT.
findings: Tree-in-bud nodules in the [ ] (endobronchial spread).
Innumerable random 2–3 mm nodules (miliary pattern).
steps.tip: Imaging distribution alone does not distinguish new infection from reactivation, establish bacillary viability/infectivity, or prove drug resistance. Actual immune/clinical context must be supplied, not inferred.

steps.label: Nodes
steps.detail: Describe every covered nodal site and source-resolved size/internal/adjacent interface; distinguish projection overlap or unresolved tissue from verified nodes.
steps.look: Inspect actual hilar/mediastinal/axillary or other covered nodal groups, attenuation/signal/enhancement/calcium or necrotic-appearing components if supported by acquired sources, airway/vessel displacement and uncovered extent.
findings: Necrotic (low-attenuation centre, rim-enhancing) mediastinal nodes.
Calcified hilar nodes (healed).
steps.tip: Necrotic-appearing/enlarged/calcified nodes have a differential. Imaging alone does not supply tissue histology, acid-fast results, genotype or resistance status.

steps.label: Pleura and airways
steps.detail: Inspect actual pleural, airway and relevant thoracic complications with source modality/phase and full obtained connections; clinical effect/organism remains separate.
steps.look: Trace effusions, pleural thickening, empyema/air/fluid or fistulous/chest-wall components, airway narrowing/bronchiectatic change and relevant pericardial/vascular/bone interfaces. Contrast, MRI, US/Doppler and other phases are separate sources only if acquired.
findings: [Right] pleural effusion.
Empyema with split pleura sign.
Bronchial stenosis.
steps.tip: Imaging fluid is not proven TB/chyle or a physiological severity measurement. Possible haemoptysis-related vascular lesions or other urgent complications require actual acquired evidence and clinical assessment.

steps.label: Sequelae and comparison
steps.detail: Record actual sequelae and matching-source change; separate apparent chronic morphology from supplied clinical/microbiological confirmation, activity, infectivity and resistance.
steps.look: Compare actual dates, matched sites, source projection/coverage/phase and treatment/clinical context. Record fibrosis/calcium/volume loss or new change; actual laboratory/specimen, molecular/culture/susceptibility and clinical source results require their own identities/dates.
findings: Apical fibrosis with volume loss and calcified granulomas (inactive, healed disease).
New cavitation compared with [date] (reactivation).
steps.tip: Scarring or calcification does not alone exclude coexisting active disease or establish noninfectivity. Normal imaging does not exclude latent infection or unavailable microscopic disease. State uncertainty and missing confirmation; do not infer successful treatment from unmatched stills.

model.reporting_aim: Partial thoracic orientation only. This companion does not supply actual patient TB lesions/cavities, full native nodal/pleural/airway/vascular/chest-wall interfaces, microscopic disease, genotype, viability, infectivity or resistance. Report actual acquired sources; unresolved anatomy and diagnostic confirmation remain unassessed.

steps.label: Location and shape
steps.detail: Localise to the thymic region and assess contour and size with the patient's age.
steps.look: Prevascular mediastinum; normal thymus is triangular or bilobed with straight or concave margins.
findings: Diffusely enlarged thymus with preserved shape (hyperplasia pattern).
Round / lobulated focal mass __ × __ mm in the thymic region.
steps.tip: Normal and rebound thymus can look mass-like in young patients; age and shape are key.

steps.label: Composition
steps.detail: Identify fat, fluid, soft tissue and calcification.
steps.look: CT attenuation.
findings: Fluid-attenuation thymic cyst.
Soft-tissue mass with calcification.
Fat, fluid and calcification (teratoma).

steps.label: MRI characterisation
steps.detail: Describe chemical-shift signal loss and T1/T2 signal.
steps.look: In- and opposed-phase MRI.
findings: Signal loss on opposed-phase images: thymic hyperplasia.
No signal loss: soft-tissue lesion such as thymoma or lymphoma.
steps.tip: Chemical-shift signal drop indicates fat within the gland and favours hyperplasia over thymoma.

steps.label: Enhancement and invasion
steps.detail: Assess enhancement and relation to vessels and pericardium.
steps.look: Contrast-enhanced images; fat planes with the great vessels and pericardium.
findings: Invasion of the [pericardium / great vessels] (invasive thymoma or thymic carcinoma).

steps.label: Pleura and nodes
steps.detail: Review pleural deposits, nodes and interval change.
steps.look: Pleural surfaces for drop metastases; nodal stations.
findings: Pleural drop metastases.
Mediastinal lymphadenopathy (thymic carcinoma or lymphoma).
Interval change since [date].
